chunks: What is microarchitecture?. The question: What is microarchitecture?
The instruction set (ISA) is the contract that says which instructions exist and what each one does.
Microarchitecture is the internal hardware design that carries them out: how many pipeline stages, what caches, how many instructions at once.
Many different microarchitectures can implement the same ISA. That is why the same software can run on a small slow chip and a large fast one.
Think of cars. The steering wheel, pedals and gearshift are the contract: any driver can use any car.
Under the hood, one car has a small economy engine and another a big turbo engine. Both obey the same controls, but they differ in speed, fuel use and cost.
Software sees only the controls. It can tell the difference only by how fast it runs.
Everything above the ISA line sees only the contract. Everything below it can change without breaking software.
Microarchitecture is the first layer under the contract and the one that sets CPI, clock, area and power.
ISA: the instructions and registers visible to software ("What is an ISA?") Pipeline: overlapping the steps of several instructions ("What is pipelining?")
In-order / out-of-order: running instructions strictly in program order, versus as soon as their inputs are ready.
Cache: a small fast memory that holds recently used data to cut waiting. CPI: average clock cycles per instruction. Fewer is better.
Run the same program of 10 to the 9 instructions on two cores that share one ISA. Core A is simple: CPI 1. 0 at 2 gigahertz, so the time is 10 to the 9 times 1.
0 over (2 times 10 to the 9) equals 0. 50 seconds. Core B has a deeper pipeline and bigger caches: CPI 1. 3 at 3 gigahertz, so the time is 10 to the 9 times 1.
3 over (3 times 10 to the 9) equals 0. 433 seconds. B is about 15% faster, but it is bigger and uses more power. Both are valid implementations.
That is the whole idea: same contract, different insides.
"Microarchitecture is how a specific processor implements its ISA: the pipeline, issue width, in-order or out-of-order execution, execution units, caches, branch predictors and buses.
The ISA is the contract software sees; the microarchitecture is the implementation and it can differ wildly while running identical programs, like an Arm Cortex-A53 versus an A76.
It's what determines CPI and clock speed, so performance, area and power, and it's chosen for the target, from tiny low-power MCUs to server cores."
